pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: src/components/about/aboutFleetModel.ts:67 The server page is the only I/O edge (one bounded, degrade-to-null read), and it passes a plain gallery prop to a pure reducer that feeds live and illustrative fleets through one AboutFleet interface, so the panes' decisions can be tested without doubles.

techniques.evidence: src/components/about/RemotionStage.tsx:131 RemotionDiagram hides the shared canvas/timing envelope (W/H/FPS/DURATION) behind a component+legend+ariaLabel interface, and RemotionStage hides the play-once/hold-last-frame/reduced-motion policy. Depth is placed where callers should not choose.

src/components/about/RemotionStage.tsx:94 The wrapper does not forward the Remotion Player's props. It pins loop/autoPlay/controls/clickToPlay and exposes only its own seven props, so the invariant (a beat, not a loop) cannot be undone by a caller.

src/components/about/FleetGrid.tsx:23 AboutFleet is a seam that is actually substituted at: fleetFrom produces both the live corpus and the labelled illustration, and the panes cannot tell which they got.

src/components/about/aboutFleetModel.ts:67 The LIVE_MIN and current-rubric decision is a pure function of a value (the module header says 'Pure, no React, client-safe'). page.tsx is the one driver that does the read.
src/app/about/page.tsx:30 The only await sits in the server page. AboutLanding and its panes are synchronous, so async does not spread into the deck.
src/components/about/aboutFleetModel.ts:72 A single-output transformation is written as filter/slice/map composition, which is the case where composition wins.

src/components/about/AboutLanding.tsx:53 Feature-to-diagram wiring is one exhaustive Record keyed by AboutFeatureId, so adding a feature fails to type-check until its diagram exists in that one place.
src/app/about/page.test.ts:89 The input (the gallery) is an ordinary constructible value, which the test builds inline. There is no host-minted type to mirror.

pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: src/components/deck/DeckNav.tsx:36 DeckNav's 'most-central entry wins' selection (a bug fix with a stated rationale) is written directly against host-minted IntersectionObserverEntry objects inside the observer callback. jsdom has no IntersectionObserver, so the effect returns at line 27, and DeckNav.test.tsx reaches none of these branches.

techniques.evidence: src/components/deck/DeckNav.tsx:36 Both mirror conditions hold: the input cannot be constructed by the test runner, and the logic has several branches. The branches the runner can reach number zero. A pure pick over {id, isIntersecting, ratio}[] would make them all reachable and leave a branchless shim.
src/components/ui/Stat.tsx:54 The accepted-value set is closed and documented ('Do not add a prop to drag them in here'), which avoids the options bag that grows one entry per caller.

src/components/ui/Surface.tsx:25 The wrapper's job is an invariant (one radius, one hairline), so it forwards a narrow Pick plus data-* attributes rather than all of HTMLAttributes, keeping style and className from overriding it.

src/components/ui/format.ts:9 The direction-tone triad is single-sourced, so a rebrand is one edit. The CSS token pairing ('Change BOTH together') is a declared two-place exception and should be noted.
src/components/deck/Reveal.tsx:75 A single-output transformation is written as a composition.
src/components/ui/format.ts:2 toneFor, fmtDelta and the other formatters are pure decisions over values with no I/O, so they are testable without doubles.
src/components/deck/Reveal.tsx:32 The code runs on two hosts (SSR and browser), but nothing in the context spawns, sleeps or times out. The only host-dependent choice is made once, in one place.

pairs.registryProposal: mirror-type-at-the-edge lists request scopes, compiler sessions, device handles and editor documents as host-minted types. Browser observer entries (IntersectionObserverEntry, ResizeObserverEntry, MutationRecord) are a very common UI-side instance: test DOMs such as jsdom do not implement the observer at all, so selection logic written in the callback is silently unreachable. Worth naming as an example.
